newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentina's Menem sees 97 growth of at least 6 pct.
newsitem.headline: Argentina's Menem sees 97 growth of at least 6 pct.

text.p: Argentina's President Carlos Menem expects gross domestic product (GDP) growth to be at least six percent this year, according to statements published Thursday by state news agency Telam.

In 1997, "GDP will grow six percent, at least, and it could surprise by coming out higher than that if (foreign) trade continues to grow, as is happening," Menem told a meeting of foreign bankers, said Telam.
Argentina's Economy Ministry has HAD officially predicted growth of five percent this year, compared with expansion of 4.4 percent in 1996.
Turning to unemployment, Menem said he was confident the jobless rate is falling.

"The unemployment index is falling. I estimate that in the next unemployment poll (due in May), the jobless will be at least between two points and three points below the last release," he said Thursday in his home town of La Rioja.
Argentina's jobless is currently at a near record high level of 17.1 percent.

Rodolfo Daer, the head of the CGT labor confederation, said in his Labor Day message that "this is a very sad day for Argentine workers, since there are two million people out of work, two million people that struggle to eat and that have no social protection."

On Wednesday, Daer had threatened the CGT may stage another 36-hour strike in addition to the one already announced for May if talks with business employers and the government do not reach any conclusions.
Menem, meanwhile, told the foreign bankers' meeting that Argentina is the country with the highest per capita income in Latin America at $9,000.
Consequently, he said, "there are big flows of workers that come here and work unofficially, being paid half of what salaried workers receive."
